text: 🇲🇽🎨 "To everyone applying to a school with an entrance exam: don’t cheat." "To all those who aspire to an educational institution with an admission exam — don’t commit any kind of fraud." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the UNAM online exam After irregularities in UNAM’s first fully virtual admission exam, Sheinbaum said the fault wasn’t the university’s but a failure to account for AI in online testing — and urged education authorities to rethink how knowledge is measured.

🇲🇽🔍 Homicides down 58% in the State of Mexico — from 6.6 a day to 2.8. Between September 2024 and June 2026, average daily homicides in Mexico’s most populous state fell 58%. High-impact crime dropped 40%. — Security report, Mañanera del Pueblo from Toluca The result of an intelligence-led strategy and the Mando Unificado Oriente deployed across 15 municipalities since June 2025 — attention to root causes, not the old "war." The 4T model, measured in numbers.

🇲🇽🌎 "We’re going to wait." Sheinbaum stays calm as Washington readies tariffs on 60 countries. "We’re going to wait. Last week the Economy Ministry presented every argument for why there shouldn’t be higher tariffs on Mexico — but we’re going to wait." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the coming US tariff round The US is weighing new tariffs on ~60 countries. Mexico already delivered its technical and commercial case. Sheinbaum receives US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at the National Palace on Thursday.

🇲🇽🏠 MEXICO'S MORTGAGE BOOK HITS A RECORD 1.5 TRILLION PESOS

Even with high interest rates, Mexico's housing-credit portfolio reached a record 1.513 trillion pesos at the end of May — up 4.9% in nominal terms from 1.442 trillion a year earlier, on Banco de México data reported by El Economista. Commercial banks now project 3–5% mortgage growth through 2026, with the market reactivating since March.

🇲🇽🛢️ 83% OF MEXICO'S GAS STATIONS NOW HOLD THE LINE ON DIESEL

8,481 gas stations — 83% of the sector — have joined the government's voluntary accord to keep diesel under 27 pesos a liter (25.39 in the border zone). Pemex backs it by feeding stations through its own last-mile distribution to cut transport costs. While global crude climbs, Mexico chose to shield the consumer, not the refiner's margin — and the 1,721 holdouts still overcharging are now the visible outliers.

🚨🇲🇽 3,300 CRIMINAL SLOT MACHINES PULLED ACROSS THE STATE OF MEXICO

In one week, authorities removed more than 3,300 slot machines across 84 of Edomex's 125 municipalities. Security chief Omar García Harfuch says cartels used them for "financing, extortion and money laundering," pulling in 600 million pesos; agents seized 10–15 million pesos in cash. The state prosecutor described the real trap: kids with no money to play were offered loans, and "when they cannot pay, they are recruited" as lookouts and dealers.

🔥🇲🇽 18.5 MILLION MEDICINES LEFT TO EXPIRE AT MEXICO'S CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL

The FGR and the Health Ministry's internal control unit are investigating how 18.5 million medications were allowed to expire at the Hospital Infantil between 2020 and 2024 — including 390,000 doses of oncology drugs like methotrexate and vincristine meant for children with cancer — a 121.4-million-peso hit to the treasury. Hospital staff filed 211 complaints in just three days of inspections.

🇲🇽🌳 MEXICO SLAMS THE DOOR ON MINING IN ALL 232 PROTECTED AREAS

Effective today, Semarnat bars every mining concession holder from exploring or extracting inside Mexico's 232 federal protected natural areas without prior environmental-impact authorization — retroactively, even for concessions granted before May 2023. Conanp will now issue a binding technical report on each request. Concessions the neoliberal era waved through now have to answer to the land.

🇲🇽🛢️ OIL HITS $80.80 — BUT WASHINGTON'S WAR PREMIUM NEVER REACHES THE PUMP

Global crude jumped to $80.80 a barrel this week — Mexico's mix closed at $80.88, above the $77.30 Hacienda budgeted. But the windfall skips Pemex: the state fuel subsidy holds gasoline at 24 pesos and diesel at 27 per liter, absorbing the spike so a war premium in the Gulf never reaches Mexican drivers. Per La Jornada, that cap is exactly what keeps domestic inflation contained.

🇲🇽📊 MEXICO'S ECONOMY SHIFTED INTO SECOND GEAR

The "Mexico is collapsing" narrative met the data again. Per El Financiero, the economy went from 0.4% growth in Q1 to 1.8% in Q2 — more than four times faster. Services, two-thirds of GDP, grew 2.2% annually in June; industry crawled back into positive territory. All of it under Trump's tariff siege and a peso the doomers keep trying to bury. Acceleration, not collapse.
